name: light_source
summary: Derived synthesis substrate — fuses SVG shape (geometry + RGB attribute_signature) + spatial_anchor (position) + frame_clock (active frame at canonical FPS) → LightSource(rgb, hsl, warmth, color_temp_k, intensity, falloff, direction, active_frames, crystal). Aggregates into WorldLightField at a (frame, fps) pair. Drops the EMISSION channel of the canonical layer_stack as a first-class queryable substrate — every harvested shape is now a candidate light.
engine_pattern: stateless synthesis. RGB→HSL pure math. McCamy-ish CCT estimation. Warmth = (r − b) modulated by green. Intensity derived from opacity × gradient_factor × stroke_boost. All crystals BLAKE3-canonical.
the_synthesis_chain: SVG shape (svg_vector_embed) + position (spatial_anchor) + frame (frame_clock) → LightSource. Adds NOTHING new to disk; everything composes existing crystals. Queryable along 4 NEW axes: by_frame, by_hue, by_proximity, by_warmth.

routing_connections.substrate_writes: none (caller persists via inference_logger or workflow card)

smoke_test_results_2026_05_28.synthesized: 4 light sources from synthetic svg attribute signatures

queryable_axes: find_lights_by_hue(target_hue, k, max_delta)  — color hue match
the_layer_stack_link: Canonical layer_stack (from workflow_card_v0 + morph_layer_polymorphism) includes 'emission'. light_source provides the queryable substrate for that channel. workflow_generator can now auto-populate emission layers from harvested shape colors + active frames.
guarantees: Deterministic — same inputs → same crystal byte-exact
Composable — every output crystal links to source_geometry_crystal + source_spatial_crystal
Frame-aware — active_frames dict pins each light to specific frame indices
Pure stdlib — no numpy, no colorsys, no PIL
usage_example:
from light_source import LightSource, WorldLightField, find_lights_near
ls = LightSource.from_svg_attribute_signature(
    attribute_signature=[1.0, 0.5, 0.1, 0,0,0, 0.9, 0.2, 0, 0],
    position=(1.0, 0.0, 2.0),
    active_frames={60: 60, 30: 30}
)
field = WorldLightField.at(60, 60, [ls])
print(field.dominant_warmth(), field.color_palette())
